thesis_text:
Bottom line: for JPMorganChase — Global Investment Banking (IBD) (Multiple, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Firm-published bar for the Summer 2027 Global Investment Banking cohort: expected graduation December 2027–June 2028 (bachelor's, or a master's completed within two years of the bachelor's), minimum cumulative GPA of 3.6 on a 4.0 scale, US work authorization (limited sponsorship noted only for STEM degrees heavily indexed in finance), English fluency, and strong analytical/accounting/finance/quantitative/modeling skills with intermediate Excel and PowerPoint (official posting, verified 2026-10-12). A finance/business/economics degree is explicitly not required, but solid numeracy is. The 3.6 is notably higher than the sophomore feeder's preferred 3.2 — the bar rises at the junior-summer step.

We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).
